bib.title: FollowIR: Evaluating and Teaching Information Retrieval Models to Follow Instructions

legacy_report:
SOURCE: FollowIR: Evaluating and Teaching Information Retrieval Models to Follow Instructions. Orion Weller, Benjamin Chang, Sean MacAvaney, Kyle Lo, Arman Cohan, Benjamin Van Durme, Dawn Lawrie, Luca Soldaini. arXiv:2403.15246v3 (7 May 2024), preprint; cs.IR. Year 2024.

COVERAGE: 17 pages. All of the extracted text (61,576 chars) was read: body, Tables 1-5, Fig 3-4 data, limitations, appendices A-E (the references were skimmed). The last ~3k chars are the Appendix E prompts, which only continue the short-instruction prompt; nothing results-bearing is missing. Figures were not extracted as images.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- claim: Most retrieval models (dense, sparse and cross-encoder) do not use instructions as a definition of relevance. They use them as keywords, and p-MRR is mostly negative.
  number: average p-MRR of BM25 -2.1, E5-base-v2 -3.9, Contriever -3.8, OpenAI v3 Large -2.7, E5-mistral -3.5, TART-Contriever -5.0
  setup: FollowIR reranking benchmark (Robust04, News21, Core17). Each model scores the query plus the original TREC instruction, then the query plus an altered, narrower instruction. p-MRR ranges from -100 to 100 and 0 means no change. Models run from 100M to 7B parameters.
  quote: "BM25 12.1 -3.1 19.3 -2.1 8.1 -1.1 13.2 -2.1" and "OpenAI v3 Large 27.2 -5.8 27.2 -2.0 21.6 -0.2 25.3 -2.7"
  where: Table 2, p.7 (offset ~19-21k)
- claim: Only models with 3B+ parameters, or instruction-tuned LMs with no retrieval training, show positive instruction following. FollowIR-7B scores best.
  number: Mistral-7B-instruct +10.1 average p-MRR; FollowIR-7B +12.2; MonoT5-3B +2.5; GritLM-7B -0.0; Google Gecko +2.3; Cohere v3 -0.2
  setup: As above. The instruct LMs act as MonoT5-style rerankers that compare true/false token probabilities.
  quote: "Generally only models with over 3B parameters or instruction-tuned LMs that haven't been trained on retrieval tasks show success at following retrieval instruction."
  where: Table 2 caption, p.7
- claim: Mechanism (keyword matching). Models do better when the instruction is cut to keywords or a short form than with the full instruction, and they cannot use the extra detail in longer instructions.
  number: none directly in the text; the sign of the effect is shown in Fig 3 and the BEIR deltas in Table 3
  setup: Ablation with query only vs keywords vs short instruction vs full instruction. GPT-4-Turbo-1106 generated the short instructions and keywords for the TREC data. For BEIR it used the original short instructions.
  quote: "These results show that models are (1) using the instruction text as keywords (as performance is higher when using only keywords) and (2) are not able to utilize the extra information in the instructions (as they generally decrease in performance with this additional information)."
  where: Section 4.3, p.8
- claim: On BEIR (SciFact, NFCorpus, FiQA), swapping a model's short instruction for domain keywords changes scores by about +/-1 point for both instruction-trained and non-instruction models. This suggests the instructions act as keywords.
  number: about +/-1 point; E5-Mistral is the exception, -5.1 on SciFact and -6.5 on FiQA. BM25 deltas: -1.7, -5.1, -1.6.
  setup: Table 3 covers only models that did poorly on instruction following. OG is the original short-instruction score. Non-instruction models were given the INSTRUCTOR/TART keywords.
  quote: "for both we see that using keywords instead of the instruction results in comparable performance (± one point)."
  where: Table 3, p.8
- claim: BM25 is a weak instruction follower, but not worse than most neural retrievers. Adding the TREC instruction does not help it, and on full-collection retrieval it can even lose points.
  number: BM25 Robust04 MAP 12.1, News21 nDCG@5 19.3, Core17 MAP 8.1 (reranking setup). Full-collection retrieval: BM25 21.4 (-1.2), 30.1 (+5.3), 16.8 (-0.2).
  setup: Table 4 reports the no-instruction score and the delta from adding the TREC instruction. The deltas for BM25 and Contriever on News21 are positive (+5.3, +9.0), while E5-base-v2 is +1.8. Everything else is negative.
  quote: "BM25 21.4 -1.2 30.1 +5.3 16.8 -0.2"
  where: Table 4, p.15
- claim: On the full retrieval collection, most retrievers lose accuracy when the long TREC instruction is added.
  number: Robust04 MAP deltas: E5-base-v2 -7.0, Contriever -7.7, TART-Contriever -10.1, BGE-base -3.1, INSTRUCTOR-XL -3.1
  setup: Full TREC collections (no reranking pool), 7 retrievers. No rerankers.
  quote: "retrieval models are not effectively using instructions and see performance degradations with longer text."
  where: Table 4 and caption, p.15
- claim: Fine-tuning Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 on about 1,800 synthetic instances gives FollowIR-7B, which improves both retrieval quality and instruction following.
  number: +6.0% relative on standard IR metrics, +20.8% relative on p-MRR; average score 23.4 to 24.8, average p-MRR +10.1 to +12.2
  setup: Training data is 1,836 TREC narrative/query pairs from tasks outside FollowIR. GPT-3.5-Turbo-1106 generated about 2 relevant and 2 non-relevant documents per query. Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 filtered the documents by whether its prediction matched the label. One relevant and one non-relevant document were kept per query, giving about 1,800 instances on about 1,200 unique query/instruction pairs. Training used LoRA with Llama-Factory.
  quote: "our model improves on both standard IR metrics (+6.0% relative improvement) and on instruction following (+20.8% relative improvement)."
  where: Section 5, p.9
- claim: On the concurrent InstructIR benchmark, FollowIR-7B has the top Robustness@10. BM25 scores lowest among the models listed.
  number: BM25 26.9; TART-Contriever 47.5; RepLLaMa 52.6; E5-Mistral 55.4; Mistral-7B-instruct 35.3; FollowIR-7B 71.5
  setup: Robustness@10 is the minimum nDCG@10 across 10 instructions for the same query. The paper calls this "Figure 4" but it is a table.
  quote: "FollowIR-7B scores double the base Mistral-7B scores (71.5 Robustness@10 vs 35.3) and is the top scoring model overall"
  where: Section 5, p.9
- claim: Strong standard-metric retrievers can still follow instructions poorly, so nDCG or MAP does not predict instruction following.
  number: OpenAI v3 Large has MAP 27.2 on Robust04 and 25.3 average, with p-MRR -2.7; GritLM-7B has 24.6 average and p-MRR 0.0; Google Gecko has 25.3 and +2.3
  setup: Table 2. API models are black boxes and their training is not known.
  quote: "API models perform strongly in terms of standard IR metrics, with OpenAI's and Google's models performing the highest overall. However, Cohere's and OpenAI's models perform poorly at instruction-following"
  where: Section 4.2, p.7
- claim: Benchmark design. TREC instructions are about 40-75 words, against about 12-17 words for queries. Prior instruction-retrieval work used instructions of fewer than 10 words, one per dataset.
  number: Table 1 |I| 40.1 / 44.0 / 68.2 words (original) and 46.9 / 53.5 / 75.2 words (altered). Queries are 15.3 / 16.6 / 11.9 words. Final query counts 32 News21, 20 Core17, 52 Robust04. Passages are 400 words with 200-word overlap, scored with MaxP. Reranking uses the top non-relevant documents from a pool of 5 models (BM25, BGE-base, E5-base-v2, TART-Contriever, INSTRUCTOR-xl).
  setup: Annotators narrowed the relevance definition so that roughly half the relevant documents became non-relevant. Only the originally relevant documents had to be re-judged.
  quote: "instructions are typically short (fewer than 10 words) and repetitive (only one instruction per dataset"
  where: Sec 1 p.2; Table 1 p.4; Sec 3 pp.4-5
- claim: The p-MRR formula. It is rank-aware, from -1 to 1, with 0 meaning no change.
  number: -1 to 1 (reported x100)
  setup: Applied to each document whose relevance was changed. Averaged within a query, then across queries.
  quote: "p-MRR = MRRog/MRRnew − 1 if Rog > Rnew; 1 − MRRnew/MRRog otherwise"
  where: Eq. 1, p.5

LIMITS
- Authors concede: (1) the setup is reranking, not full retrieval, because each retriever would find different relevant documents; full-corpus results (Appendix C, Table 4) cover only 7 models and no rerankers, and are said to trend similarly. (2) TREC judgements were not checked for errors, and the new annotations "may have small errors".
- Not shown: query counts are small (20-52 per collection; the paper says 30-50 is standard in IR). All data are news corpora (Washington Post, NYT, Robust04 news). The training data is synthetic (GPT-3.5) and small. The keyword-ablation keywords and short instructions come from GPT-4. No hybrid or BM25 plus dense fusion is tested. No evidence on chunk-level RAG, though passages are 400-word. p-MRR is relative to each model's own ranking, so it does not measure absolute quality. Table 3 omits the strong instruction followers. Results are from 2024 and newer instruction-following retrievers are not covered.
- Relevance to the target note: the paper does not directly compare keyword vs semantic vs hybrid search. BM25 appears only as one baseline among the "no-instruction" models.

BUILDS ON: TREC narratives (Voorhees 2005 Robust04; Allan et al. 2017 Core; Soboroff et al. 2020 News). Instruction retrieval: Su et al. 2022 (INSTRUCTOR), Asai et al. 2022 (TART), Wang et al. 2023a (E5-Mistral), Muennighoff et al. 2024 (GritLM), Xiao et al. 2023 (BGE). Concurrent: Oh et al. 2024 (InstructIR). Benchmarks: BEIR (Thakur et al. 2021), MTEB (Muennighoff et al. 2022). Methods: MaxP (Dai & Callan 2019), MonoT5 (Nogueira et al. 2020), BM25 (Robertson et al. 1995), LoRA (Hu et al. 2021), Llama-Factory (Hiyouga 2023), Mistral-Instruct (Jiang et al. 2023), Weller et al. 2024 (NevIR, negation).

CODE: none worth keeping, apart from the p-MRR formula quoted above. Code and data are at github.com/orionw/FollowIR (footnote 3, p.3).

FIGURES (not extracted as images; captions from the text)
- Fig 1 (p.2): how queries and TREC instructions differ (more detail, less background, negation).
- Fig 2 (p.3): pairwise evaluation. Same query, original vs altered instruction, and the ranking should change.
- Fig 3 (p.7): score change from keyword, short and full instructions. It shows the keyword mechanism most clearly.
- "Figure 4" (p.9): the InstructIR Robustness@10 table.

PROBLEMS: Table 2 and Fig 3 extracted as plain text, so the Fig 3 bar values are not readable. The Table 3 columns "OG" and "∆ w/Key." line up in order. The Table 4 caption is garbled but readable. The paper says its p-MRR table is "Table 2" and the keyword ablation of TREC (Fig 3) has no numbers in the text. No embedded instructions were found in the PDF.
